facts: A large molasses storage tank burst in Boston on January 15, 1919.
A fast-moving wave of molasses swept through the North End.
The disaster killed 21 people and injured about 150.

The flood killed 21 people and injured about 150.

topic: The shortest war in recorded history
facts: Britain and Zanzibar fought on August 27, 1896.
The conflict lasted less than an hour.
It followed a dispute over who would become sultan after Hamad bin Thuwaini died.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Anglo-Zanzibar War
facts: The Anglo-Zanzibar War was fought on August 27, 1896.
It lasted no longer than 40 minutes.

sources.title: Historic Royal Palaces: Anglo-Zanzibar War
facts: The war was extremely brief and followed a succession dispute in Zanzibar.

topic: When London held fairs on the frozen River Thames
facts: During especially cold winters, the River Thames sometimes froze solid enough to support crowds.
People set up booths, food stalls and entertainments on the ice.
The last major frost fair took place in 1814.

sources.title: Historic UK: The Thames Frost Fairs
facts: Fairs and entertainments were held on the frozen Thames.
The last frost fair was in 1814.

sources.title: Royal Museums Greenwich: Frost fairs on the River Thames
facts: The Thames froze during severe winters and people gathered on the ice.
The ice hosted stalls and entertainment.
Global temperatures fell in 1816 after the 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora.
Cold and abnormal weather damaged crops in parts of Europe and North America.
The period became known as the Year Without a Summer.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Year Without a Summer
facts: The year 1816 was marked by unusually cold weather.
The 1815 Tambora eruption contributed to the cooling.

sources.title: NASA Earth Observatory: Global Effects of Mount Tambora
facts: Tambora's 1815 eruption affected global climate.
Cold weather and crop failures followed in 1816.

topic: The ancient Roman fast-food counter preserved at Pompeii
facts: Archaeologists excavated a decorated thermopolium at Pompeii.
Thermopolia sold ready-to-eat food and drinks from counters fitted with large jars.
The site was preserved when Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE.

sources.title: Archaeological Park of Pompeii: Thermopolium of Regio V
facts: The Regio V thermopolium had a decorated counter and containers for food.
It served food and drink in ancient Pompeii.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Pompeii
facts: Pompeii was buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE.
In 1518, people in Strasbourg danced uncontrollably for days or weeks.
Authorities initially responded by providing spaces and musicians for dancing.
The cause remains debated and uncertain.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Dancing plague of 1518
facts: A dancing mania occurred in Strasbourg in 1518.
Its cause remains uncertain.

sources.title: History Today: Dancing Plague of Strasbourg
facts: The outbreak began in Strasbourg in 1518 and authorities encouraged dancing before changing course.
